stops.narrative: Begin with the relationship between grain, food preparation and people doing work. Keep Giza’s excavated workplaces, the translated crew record and the selected Saqqara chapel wall distinct. A recurring task requires more than a finished monument.

Follow the guide from space through subdivision to fill and renewal. The project describes woven stone-filled bags and changing rooms; it does not supply every builder’s choices or one sequence for all buildings. Compare the material tasks before inferring the same institution.

Imagine bringing fuel from the entrance toward the hearth in the independently drawn feature guide. Then read how House 1 changed during modern rebuilding. Physical features support practical questions while their present arrangement also has a history.

conclusion: Preparing food, renewing buildings and maintaining domestic space depended on people, materials and organization. The evidence here makes particular relationships visible without identifying every worker or establishing a common government across these places.

evidence.prompt: How could we investigate the recurring work that kept these places usable?

options.text: Match a practical task to its specific record, then test the interpretation with further evidence.
options.feedback: A workplace, construction fill and a described house each support different questions. Their limits help choose a further source rather than erase the work they reveal.
